newsitem.title: UK: UK's Lasmo sees strong production growth.
newsitem.headline: UK's Lasmo sees strong production growth.

text.p: Oil exploration and production company Lasmo Plc said on Thursday it expects production to grow strongly to around 250,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2001.

The company earlier reported that net profit before exceptional items in the first half of 1997 rose to 26 million pounds ($42.5 million) from 24 million, coming in at the low end of analysts' expectations.
Recent exploration success and development of the core areas in Britain, Indonesia, North Africa, Pakistan and Venezuela will fuel production in coming years, Lasmo said.
Production in the first half of 1997 was 171,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, which was comparable to the same 1996 period.
Higher production in Britain was offset by lower output in Indonesia, said Lasmo, which is Britain's second biggest oil exploration and production firm.

Production was slightly lower than expected due to delays in the start-up of the North Sea MacCulloch field, but Lasmo said it is still on track to reach its target of 200,000 barrels per day by year end. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
